scope: Independent geographic audit of all 169 existing discoveries, eight rendered landmark anchors, and both source-based Lakefront Trail routes. Canceled water cribs excluded.
method: Resolve every coordinate URL in the independently cached named OSM index, then reparse the original OSM XML features and coordinates.
Assemble multipolygon outer and inner rings by original node IDs; test pin containment with holes. Closed artwork and bridge ways are areas, not centerlines.
Measure named-node/line distances, recompute claimed area centroids, check map bounds and every pair of discovery coordinates.
Review source-name identity and explicitly distinguish broad parks, paired sculptures and building anchors from entrances.
Compare all 253 exported trail-way coordinates and node IDs directly with original XML; compare relation membership and independently calculate connected components.

limitations: OSM geometry is community mapping, not an on-site survey; matching it does not establish centimeter-level real-world accuracy.

This is a fresh audit of independent cached source XML. It does not claim a new aerial survey or live verification of temporary closures, current entrance access, construction or every official website.
Historical original-pin displacements and point-meaning notes are included only as context from the earlier audit, never as independent proof of correct geometry.
The visual-anchor review checks geographic placement and the Navy Pier footprint; it does not certify every architectural detail of generated illustrations.
Some discoveries deliberately represent a broad park, a complex, paired artworks or a named subarea; their documented coordinates are not routing entrances.
